title: A worker's session can start real paid claude sessions: nothing in its environment stops a smoke test from calling claude
goal: dispatch starts the worker's own session by the absolute path of the claude it found and gives the session a PATH whose first directory is stub-bin under the item's scratch directory, holding a stub claude (a /bin/sh script written by dispatch) that prints to stderr the item id and that it needs an answered gate naming money and exits 2, unless the item carries a gate with an answer for which bl_authority.strict_signals lists a money signal, when the PATH is unchanged, so a worker's child call of claude reaches the real binary only for an item whose spend the operator approved, in new, resumed and begun dispatches alike

run:
import glob, json, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
def run(gated):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        bindir = os.path.join(d, "bin"); os.mkdir(bindir)
        mark = os.path.join(d, "paid-call-made"); ok = os.path.join(d, "ok.json"); rc = os.path.join(d, "rc"); err = os.path.join(d, "err")
        open(ok, "w").write(json.dumps({"is_error": False, "session_id": "s"}))
        script = "#!/bin/sh\ncase " + chr(34) + chr(36) + "* " + chr(34) + " in\n".replace("* ", "*")
        script += "  *--add-dir*) cat >/dev/null; claude -p smoke-test >/dev/null 2>" + err + "; echo " + chr(36) + "? > " + rc + "; cat " + ok + " ;;\n  *smoke-test*) echo called >> " + mark + " ;;\nesac\n"
        open(os.path.join(bindir, "claude"), "w").write(script)
        os.chmod(os.path.join(bindir, "claude"), 0o755)
        env = dict(os.environ, PATH=bindir + os.pathsep + os.environ["PATH"], KB_COORD_STORE=os.path.join(d, "coord.sqlite"))
        origin = os.path.join(d, "origin.git")
        subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", "--bare", "-b", "main", origin], check=True)
        root = os.path.join(d, "root"); os.mkdir(root)
        g = lambda *a: subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, *a], capture_output=True, text=True)
        bl = lambda *a: subprocess.run([sys.executable, "_tools/backlog.py", "--root", root, *a], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env, timeout=120)
        g("init", "-q", "-b", "main"); g("config", "user.email", "x@example.com"); g("config", "user.name", "x"); g("remote", "add", "origin", origin)
        open(os.path.join(root, "README"), "w").write("x\n"); g("add", "."); g("commit", "-qm", "init"); g("push", "-q", "origin", "main")
        iid = bl("new", "story", "--title", "T", "--goal", "g", "--touch", "f.txt", "--check", "python3 -c pass").stdout.split()[2]
        path = glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "**", iid + ".json"), recursive=True)[0]
        item = json.load(open(path)); item["status"] = "todo"
        if gated:
            item["gates"] = [{"id": "g1", "kind": "blocking", "question": "Approve USD 1 of paid model calls for the smoke test?", "options": ["approve", "refuse"], "recommendation": "approve", "class": "money", "answer": "approve", "by": "operator", "operator": "op-00000000", "role": "interactive"}]
        json.dump(item, open(path, "w"))
        g("add", "."); g("commit", "-qm", "plant todo"); g("push", "-q", "origin", "main")
        if bl("claim", iid, "--by", "claude-aaaaaaaa").returncode:
            sys.exit("claim failed")
        r = bl("dispatch", iid)
        if r.returncode:
            sys.exit("dispatch failed: " + (r.stdout + r.stderr)[-300:])
        read = lambda p: open(p).read() if os.path.exists(p) else ""
        return os.path.exists(mark), read(rc).strip(), read(err), iid
reached, code, text, iid = run(False)
if reached:
    sys.exit("a worker with no approved spend gate reached the real claude")
if code != "2" or iid not in text:
    sys.exit("the stub did not exit 2 naming the item: " + repr((code, text[-200:])))
if not run(True)[0]:
    sys.exit("a worker whose item carries an answered money gate was cut off from the real claude")

gates.question: Does any answer to a gate naming a cost signal count as approval for the stub, or only an affirmative one?
options: any answer, as the goal words it
only an answer that is not a refusal
gates.recommendation: any answer, as the goal words it
gates.reason: the goal says an answer for which strict_signals lists a money signal, and no answer text can be parsed reliably
gates.answer: any answer, as the goal words it

notes: Retro finding of the drain: ST-i5az334d's worker started 4 real Haiku 5.5 sessions (about 0.011 USD) as a smoke test though only other items of the sprint had an approved spend; the brief's rule on spending is text only. Premise (reproduces: the repro): worker_env (bl_dispatch.py) passes the dispatching session's PATH, so a worker's child call of claude reaches the real binary whatever its item's gates say. The stub is the retro's first example; the other, a spend check at done, would find the spend only afterwards and is left to the planner. Popen resolves argv[0] with the PATH it is given, so the stub directory must go on the PATH only after dispatch has resolved the real claude to a path; worker_env is also called by bench_load.py: keep its signature compatible. The repro plants a fake claude as the dispatched binary and as its child's target (no model call). Related: ST-ybksk2f2 (the opposite rule: an item whose code starts claude -p proves one capped real call). Planner settled the worker's choices so none becomes a blocking gate: the stub lives in stub-bin of the item's scratch directory and is written by dispatch at each start, approval is any gate of the item with an answer whose strict_signals include money (a public helper of bl_authority, no change there), worker_env keeps its signature (bench_load.py calls it). Check: the repro runs both cases (no gate: the paid call is stopped, an answered money gate: it reaches the real binary). Run order dependency dropped at 20:10 (landings take about 45 minutes each; the planned chain would not finish before the sprint's worker cutoff). Rebase merges separate hunks of the shared file.
